processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Aged at 530 °C for 22 h; Table IV hardness 304 ± 13 BHN and dynamic fracture toughness 242 ± 82 kJ/m². Preceded by solution treatment at 1050 °C 2 h (parent process proc_st-1050c-2h).
Aged 60 h at 530 °C; used for carbon partitioning coefficient measurement (2.1 in κ-carbide) and predicted yield-strength increase of 120 MPa/wt.% Si.
Aged at 530 °C for 90 h; Table IV hardness 366 ± 9 BHN and dynamic fracture toughness 95 ± 15 kJ/m².

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix hardened by homogeneous, coherent precipitation of nanosized κ-carbide ((Fe,Mn)3AlCx, E2₁ cubic perovskite) formed via spinodal decomposition/ordering during 530 °C aging.

phases_present.morphology: nanosized coherent precipitates; cuboidal, transitioning to plate morphologies along elastically soft <100>

defects.porosity: more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel

inclusions.type: AlN, MnS, Al-N-Mn-O and other oxide/sulfide inclusions; micro-defects (porosity) dominate

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Shearing of κ-carbides during plastic deformation forms planar slip bands, causing loss of strain hardening and toughness, and increases propensity for {111} glide-plane decohesion at high strain rates.

interfaces.slip_behavior: planar slip facilitated by κ-carbide precipitation; increases {111} glide-plane decohesion propensity especially at high strain rates
interfaces.phase_evolution: spinodal decomposition → short-range ordering → coarsening; cuboidal κ-carbide transitions to plate morphology along elastically soft <100>

unmapped_findings: Carbon partitioning coefficient of carbon in κ-carbide = 2.1 for the 0.59% Si steel aged 60 h at 530 °C (versus 2.9 for the 1.56% Si steel); silicon partitions to austenite during aging and decreases the austenite lattice parameter, increasing the κ–γ constrained mismatch (b0021).

Age-hardened 0.59% Si (0.002% P) specimens showed the lowest dynamic fracture toughness among the low-phosphorus silicon-containing steels in Table IV, which the authors attribute to a larger amount of porosity (b0079).

Porosity (micro-defects) in the 0.59% Si steel was more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel; total inclusion density was similar among the three low-P silicon steels at 62–78 inclusions/mm² (b0079, Figure 15).

Parent solution-treated condition (1050 °C 2 h) of the same 0.59% Si, 0.002% P alloy: hardness 200 ± 10 BHN and dynamic fracture toughness 715 kJ/m² (Table IV, b0075). This belongs to the solution-treated (parent) process, not the aged condition.
Solution-treated 0.59% Si steel shows no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite, regardless of Si content, as confirmed by XRD and TEM (b0021).
